records.title: Mackensen receipt request through Nikolajew, with literal reference fields
records.header_literal: A) FUER UKS v LP (5.10 p.m., November 2nd); 1530 (2/11); RICHI-300
records.readable_german: An Oberkdo. Mackensen. Empfangsbestaetigung von RM. 1. A. A1118 GEH. OP. und RM. 1. A. 111M7 GEH. OP. ueber Nikolajew durch F. T. erbeten. OHL. RM. 1. A. No. 104716 GEW. OP.
records.meaning: The message requests radio confirmation through Nikolajew that Mackensen command received the two referenced communications. The raw reference strings A1118 and 111M7, and the final GEW designation, are preserved.
notes: This physical record is section A; the original p105 challenge concerns the different 290-slot section B and retains its identifier and earlier attribution.

All 300 source slots are retained in the printed order. The earlier 308-slot OCR block included seven characters from the next header and expanded printed DXXXX to six characters; correcting the machine transcription is not an alteration of the historical ciphertext.
The primary readable display changes spacing and punctuation only. A1118, 111M7 and GEW are not silently converted to more familiar references.

A separately priced interpretation compares the two references with independent p105 C1 and p106 A2; agreement of subject matter supports a reference-identification hypothesis, not an assertion that the telegrams are identical copies.

prior_credit: Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier repository OCR and unchanged-key outputs are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. No universal first-decipherment priority is asserted.
limits: All native source slots remain in printed order; no insertion, deletion or reordering.
Unknown square cells remain globally coupled and injective. Roundtrip completion witnesses are explicitly nonhistorical.
Observed-coordinate substitutions and source-mask fills are priced separately. A source-compatible word proposal is not proof of unique historical wording.
